items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: Hilton Jefferson and I had baritones when we worked with Fletcher

ctx.x: Yeah. Benny Carter, he was great. He started that four-part harmony in 1929, 1930, which was, you know, just about unheard of. It just came into style, and like I said, about piano players and banjo and guitar players and whatever, you know, it was a complete turnaround because before that they were just playing triads mostly, played triads.

But Benny -- but Benny -- of course he played saxophone, then he had three in the section, so:that made four saxophones, which was a tenor and three altos. Then later on, I think Duke Ellington was the first, one of the first -- I can't actually say that he was the first -- to add a baritone to the saxophone section. Of course Fletcher, we had baritones, Hilton Jefferson and I had baritones when we worked with Fletcher, but they were just doubles. We weren't baritone players as such all the time, and the…
But then when I joined Kirby's band I had the baritone there too for awhile, but I just played choruses, solos on it, you know, because the music was written for the alto.
